clue.text: Accept unpleasant consequences of looking at score?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for taking your punishment
second meaning, read literally: turning your face towards printed music

explanation.surface: Someone is reckoning with the fallout from studying a match result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' reads as a sporting result, but here it is a musical score, which is what a musician faces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to confront the penalty for your own actions; taken literally the phrase describes a musician reading sheet music.

clue.text: Pay for man engaged to cover first night

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece sits around another

parts.note: a man engaged to be married

indicators.note: first asks for just the opening letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: the first letter of night

explanation.surface: A fiancé foots the bill for an opening-night performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To finance something is to provide the money for it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Flier landed commanding officer first — about time!

parts.note: standard abbreviation for commanding officer

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word is placed around a letter

parts.note: alit is a past tense of alight, to land
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An officer finally touches down and someone cries that it took long enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' tells you the officer's letters lead, and the time goes inside the word for landed. Flier is a crossword favourite for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The coal tit is a small bird, and a bird is a flier.

clue.text: Badly treating little hobo?

parts.note: a hobo is a tramp, a homeless wanderer
-ling is a suffix for a small one, as in duckling

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of mistreating a small vagrant.
explanation.walkthrough: The diminutive suffix -ling turns a tramp into a little tramp, giving a word that also means stamping on.
explanation.definitionFit: Trampling on someone, figuratively, is treating them harshly and with contempt.

clue.text: Lets student off for rests

indicators.note: off means taken away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to let a property is to lease it
L is a learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A landlord allows a tenant off the hook in exchange for a break.
explanation.walkthrough: LEASES loses its L, the learner.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off or ease up is to relax effort, which is to rest.

clue.text: College plunging right into argument against mythical creature

parts.note: short for university

indicators.note: something plunging into another goes inside it

parts.note: the cons are the arguments against, as in pros and cons
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A college gets dragged into a debate against belief in legends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Argument against' is a single unit: the con of pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is a legendary horse with one horn, a creature of myth.

clue.text: Don't draw a single conclusion — not a thing — about Dante's work

indicators.note: not a says the word after it must be left out of the phrase before

parts.note: to draw no conclusion at all is to infer nothing
the word to be dropped

explanation.surface: A critic warns against reaching firm conclusions about the Divine Comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: INFER NOTHING with THING removed leaves INFERNO.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferno is the first part of Dante's Divine Comedy, his journey through Hell.

clue.text: North of the border, horse-drawn cart returned to police station

parts.note: Scotland lies north of the border with England

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read in the other direction

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads, pulled by horses

explanation.surface: A Scottish horse-drawn cart is taken back to the cop shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the London headquarters of the Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland Yard is the name of the Metropolitan Police headquarters in London, a famous police station.

clue.text: Vocal composition is competent thanks to volunteers

parts.note: one who can is able
ta is informal British for thanks
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve; to adds it on

explanation.surface: A choir piece is performed well thanks to amateur singers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is the British part-time volunteer force.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a sung work for voices and instruments, so a piece of vocal music.

clue.text: Smell 50% less with a bit of a cold

indicators.note: fifty per cent means only half of the following word is kept

parts.note: to smell something is to sniff it
only its first half stays

explanation.surface: With a slight cold your sense of smell is halved.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniffle is a slight cold, the kind that makes you sniff repeatedly.

clue.text: Occasionally even Tory foes reform!

indicators.note: to reform is to form again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Now and then even the Conservatives' opponents mend their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Every so often is an idiom meaning from time to time, not regularly.

clue.text: Brown knit best for pullover

parts.note: tan is a light brown
K is the knitting-pattern abbreviation for knit
the top one is the best

explanation.surface: A brown knitted garment is chosen as the finest sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: In knitting patterns K stands for knit and P for purl.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank top is a sleeveless knitted jumper pulled on over the head, a type of pullover.

clue.text: Flog small company to old city gent: no books required

indicators.note: no means without, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
Co is the abbreviation for company
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A small firm sells off to an elderly urban gentleman who needs no reading matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' looks like sell, but it is the definition in the sense of whip. GENT loses NT.
explanation.definitionFit: To scourge is to whip someone, and flog also means to beat with a whip.

clue.text: Expert has criminal taped

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A specialist has a crook caught on tape.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept as a noun is a skilled person, a synonym for an expert.

clue.text: Cruel irony finding gap in list supposedly including everything

indicators.note: finding something in a place means it sits inside, so one piece goes within another
cruel suggests twisted treatment, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
a vent is an opening or gap

explanation.surface: Someone notes the harsh irony of spotting an omission in a supposedly complete list.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters split around the gap word, which sits in the middle of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventory is a complete itemised list of goods or property.

clue.text: Lobby against sub-elite organisation

parts.note: V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: organisation means arranging things afresh, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Pressure groups campaign against a second-tier elite body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobby' looks like a verb for campaigning, but it is the noun for an entrance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestibule is an entrance hall, which is what a lobby is.

clue.text: Drives out underworld secret societies

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
Freemasons meet in lodges

explanation.surface: Hidden criminal fraternities force rivals out.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge is to force something out of its position, synonymous with driving it out.

clue.text: Vegetable's a bit crisp in a Chinese restaurant

indicators.note: a bit of something is just a part of it, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: A Chinese restaurant serves its greens crisp.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green plant eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Watch old boy attend to customers

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil
to serve customers is to attend to them

explanation.surface: A former pupil keeps an eye on customers being served.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to watch closely, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Chap set off for fruit

parts.note: a chap is a man
to set off is to go

explanation.surface: A man heads off to buy fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is a tropical stone fruit.

clue.text: Mafioso gang takes out rest

parts.note: a mob is a gang

indicators.note: out suggests disorder or being put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A criminal gang removes someone from their break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes out' looks like a single gangster phrase for killing, but out is the anagram signal on rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mafioso is a member of the Mafia, a gangster or mobster.

clue.text: With old ones coming in, check up when the volume's higher

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so these letters go inside another word
in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
O is the abbreviation for old
I is the Roman one, so ones are I's

explanation.surface: Old ones arriving makes the room louder after a check.
explanation.walkthrough: Ones are Roman numeral I's, so the plural gives two letters; in a down clue 'up' turns the check word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisier is the comparative of noisy, describing a place or thing at greater volume.

clue.text: Sail sea freely using different names

indicators.note: freely means without fixed order, so the letters can be arranged anew

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone sails the ocean freely under false identities.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliases are assumed names, used in place of a person's real one.

clue.text: Pits us in return against politicians

indicators.note: in return means coming back, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: taken as written
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone sets us against politicians in retaliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pits' looks like a verb, as in pitting one side against another, but it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumps are pits or wells that collect drainage, so they are pits.

clue.text: Information about cheese is put concisely

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is wrapped round another

parts.note: INF is a short form of information
Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: Details about a cheese are given briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: In brief is an idiom meaning in few words, said concisely.

clue.text: Where Taj Mahal is in poorly lit sketch?

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: dim means badly lit
the Taj Mahal stands in Agra, India

explanation.surface: A drawing of a famous monument made in bad light.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a simple explanatory drawing, a kind of sketch.

clue.text: Straighten out relative with no head for drink

indicators.note: having no head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: A beheaded relative is offered alcohol as a corrective.
explanation.walkthrough: AUNT loses its first letter to leave UNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To untwine is to unwind twisted strands, straightening them out.

clue.text: Does he only fleece timid people?

definitions.text: Does he only fleece timid people?

parts.note: surface reading: a swindler who cheats only the meek and easily led
setter's reading: removing wool, and timid people are sheep in the figurative sense

explanation.walkthrough: Fleece looks like swindle, and sheep is slang for timid followers; read literally, the one who fleeces sheep is a farm worker.
explanation.definitionFit: This farm worker clips the wool from flocks, and the meek followers of the surface are figuratively a flock.
